strengths_deep_dive: The Muslim Association of Puget Sound maintains a balanced operational model with significant program expenditure. In FY2024, MAPS reported <cite id="[1]">$7,286,362 in total revenue</cite> and directed <cite id="[1]">82.4% of expenses to program services</cite>, exceeding the standard 75% sector benchmark [1]. The organization benefits from strong financial reserves, holding <cite id="[9]">17.3 months of working capital in reserve</cite>, which protects core educational and community programs during economic fluctuations [9]. Additionally, Charity Navigator awards MAPS <cite id="[9]">an overall rating of 86/100</cite>, reflecting solid fiscal management and transparency in core financial reporting [9].
rich_narrative.summary: The Muslim Association of Puget Sound (MAPS) provides religious education, daily prayer services, and community programming across the Puget Sound region. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="[1]">$7,286,362 in total revenue</cite> to support its local programs [1]. MAPS offers structured programs through the PNW Seminary for adults studying Islamic scholarship and leadership, alongside community support initiatives such as the MAPS-MCRC service branch and the Small Business Resiliency Network [3]. Financial filings from FY2024 show that the charity directed <cite id="[1]">82.4% of its expenses to program services</cite>, meeting standard benchmarks for financial allocation [1]. The organization holds <cite id="[2]">an overall score of 86.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite>, backed by 17.3 months of working capital reserves that provide operational stability [9]. However, evaluations reveal gaps in formal governance documentation, as board member disclosures and specific governance policies remain unverified in public filings [1]. Furthermore, while MAPS delivers direct services within its local region, its operational footprint remains geographically concentrated in Washington State [3].
